active_questions.q: For which E. coli regulatory circuits does the literature provide activator binding-site evidence strong enough to build a PWM from?
What network motifs recur across transcriptional regulatory networks, and what dynamic behaviour does each motif produce?
active_questions._acquisition_note: First-pass swept 2026-08-09 (GLMP_MASTER_TODO.md item 53, resumed sweeps). Question-text scoring (no natural anchor candidate in `flagged`); cutoff 0.395, set by title-sampling at 1-point percentile resolution -- falloff was noisier than glmp-q5's: off-topic content (immune/disease/PPI/physiological networks) appears as early as p21, genuine bacterial-regulatory-network content dominates again through p35, then trends off-topic from p36. 2,468 papers written (2,219 new, 249 merged onto existing corpus docs).

active_questions.q: Which regulatory circuits exhibit bistability or switch-like behaviour, and what evidence establishes the switch rather than a graded response?
active_questions._acquisition_note: First-pass swept 2026-08-09. 'Switch' is a heavily overloaded word: false positives from immunology (antibody class-switch recombination), chemistry, and optogenetics appear interleaved with genuine bistability content rather than cleanly separated (unlike glmp-q3's recovery-then-off pattern). 5-point percentile-block title reading found the on-topic majority ends around p27/p28 and never clearly regains it. Cutoff 0.375 -> 1,241 papers (963 new, 278 merged). One paper (pubmed_19910671) legitimately qualifies for both glmp-q3 and glmp-q4.

active_questions.q: How are bacterial stress-response regulons organised, and what governs the transition between the resting and induced state?
active_questions._acquisition_note: First-pass swept 2026-08-10. Cleanest falloff of the three questions swept so far -- specific bacterial-biology vocabulary, unambiguous on-topic content through ~p70, real transition at ~p74. Cutoff 0.36 -> 3,583 papers (3,532 new, 51 merged), the largest single-question write in this expansion (74% of candidates passed, vs. 27-36% for glmp-q3/q4).

active_questions.q: How do two-component systems and phosphorelays transduce signals into transcriptional output?
active_questions._acquisition_note: First-pass swept 2026-08-10/11. Largest candidate pool so far (19,745 -- two-component systems and quorum sensing are both large fields). 'two-component system' hit PubMed's retstart>9998 ceiling (disclosed, pre-existing instrument limit). Falloff: unambiguous through ~p28, mixed zone (chemistry/physics 'component'/'system' homonyms) with genuine content still frequent through ~p62, decisively off from p63. Cutoff 0.27 -> 12,400 papers (11,711 new, 689 merged), by far the largest single write in this expansion.
